objective: Choose the S1 field-inversion regularization from prior theory rather than from convention, and report posterior uncertainty on the correction field instead of a point field, using the regularization provenance the weighted arm already wrote down as the design input
rationale: The S1 line closed end to end with both gates failing for measured reasons and with the successor arm filed, unrun, and its trigger routed explicitly to this design phase, so this item is not a new idea but the named unblock of an existing hold. The material it needs is already tabulated. The provenance table carries three runs with their objective weights and their penalty weights, the ground each was chosen on, and the achieved penalty share, and all three sit below the convention the reference method uses, which is the honest way of saying the choices were made by defensible habit rather than by theory. The Bayesian reading is already written into the same record: the penalty toward unity is a Gaussian prior on the correction field whose precision is set by the penalty weight and the noise scale, the bounds truncate that prior, and between 212 and 224 cells sit on the lower bound in every converged field, which is exactly the posterior mass a truncation hides and a point field cannot show. Better still, the record contains an observation a posterior treatment can be graded against rather than merely compared with: in the first run the optimisation plateaued where the penalty gradient and the objective gradient cancelled at a norm ratio near unity, with a root-mean-square near 0.0165, and the record names that as the calibration point a posterior treatment should reproduce. The failed gates give the design its shape too. The first gate missed at 0.05713 against a bar of 0.05320, a factor of 1.074, while still descending at roughly 0.004 per evaluation when the budget guard stopped it, so the loss was not converged and a posterior built at that point must say so. The second gate reports 42.7 percent inside the metric window against 79.7 percent inside the loss support, which is the loss-support versus metric-support question the held arm exists to answer and which a prior specification has to decide anyway. Axis A: reading-kind, priced from measured per-evaluation cost on this exact case. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0, and the in-sample position is stated below.

cost_basis: REPRICED 2026-08-11 by the pre-registration (the S1 priors pre-registration, section 5), which found the filed 150 underpriced for this item's own posterior gate. Measured on this exact case: ~20 core-min per compute_totals evaluation at -primalTol 1e-8 and --cpus=2 (weighted arm billed 19-20 uncontended over 7 evaluations; reinversion billed 320.13 over 16), ~8-9 core-min for a final-state cold control plus field and cell-centre write-out (measured 8.10 and 8.54). Budget: MAP arm under the derived prior, warm-started from the existing beta_final, 6 evaluations = ~120; final-state control and write-out = ~9; six Hessian-vector products for the low-rank posterior, one-sided finite difference of the adjoint gradient sharing the MAP gradient so one evaluation each = ~120; total ~249 against a 260 hard cap. The prior derivation, the noise-scale estimate, the provenance table and the plateau-balance re-basing are already DONE at zero solver core-min on fields already written, so they are not in this price. The reason 150 does not work: per-cell credible intervals over 21,000 parameters need curvature, this stack exposes gradients, so curvature costs gradient evaluations; 150 buys the arm and about one Hessian-vector product.
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes with different consequences, and the falsifiers are named in the pre-registration section 6 so the stage can fail. One: the posterior credible intervals straddle unity in a majority of separated-flow window cells, which would mean the measured 94.9 percent window error reduction is a fit the data does not constrain and the point field cannot be published as an identified correction. Two: the leading prior-preconditioned Hessian eigenvalues show no decay, which would mean the problem is not effectively low-dimensional, no affordable finite-rank posterior is defensible, and the obstruction is the parameterization rather than the objective or the prior, promoting the Dow-style nu_t-discrepancy alternative from named to indicated. Three: the derived prior collapses the window fix below 50 percent reduction, which would mean the correction was carried by an almost-flat prior doing load-bearing work nobody accounted for. The merely disappointing outcome, distinct from all three, is that the derived weight lands near the value in use, the pinning drops as predicted, and the gates land where they already are -- confirming the convention was defensible by luck, and giving this line its first derived prior. Either way the truncated prior mass gets a number: the weight in use corresponds to a Gaussian prior with standard deviation 0.676 on a positive multiplier, which places 6.96 percent of its mass on physically impossible negative production and 11.85 percent below the pre-registered lower bound.
in_sample_verdict: Clean, and the boundary is the same one the S1 line has carried throughout. The inversion runs on the backward-facing-step training case, no scored test case is opened, and no scoring call is made. The posterior is a statement about the correction field on that case; if any later filing proposes carrying it to a scored case, that filing owes its own in-sample verdict and this one does not grant it.

gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Bayesian inverse problems: Stuart's acta numerica / Kaipio-Somersalo -> PROOF: S1's regularization chosen by theory (prior interpretation), posterior uncertainty on beta reported, not just a point field.' Operationalised into four pre-registered gates in S1_PRIORS_PREREGISTRATION.md section 4, all required. G-P1: the penalty weight is derived from a stated prior and a measured noise scale, reported against the three values already used and across the pre-registered noise band; a value chosen to match a previous run fails. Note the derivation is already executed and lands at 8.13e-06, which is 0.81x the 1e-05 in use, so the MAGNITUDE agreeing with convention is pre-declared and cannot later be presented as a derivation triumph -- the experiment is the prior's FORM. G-P2: the lognormal prior's restoring pull at the lower bound is 8.2x the Gaussian's, so the pre-stated prediction is that cells pinned at 0.2 fall from 223 to fewer than 60; PASS below 60, graded a wrong prediction at or above 223. G-P3: the reported product is per-cell credible intervals over all 21,000 cells plus the truncation mass plus the leading prior-preconditioned Hessian spectrum the intervals were built from; asserted error bars fail. G-P4 [CORRECTED 2026-08-11, commit 57fd0d83 -- the re-basing this field previously described is WITHDRAWN and the canonical statement is S1_PRIORS_PREREGISTRATION section 4, which this field must not be read against]: the posterior reproduces the corrupted run's plateau balance stated as the RATIO AND THE COSINE at the plateau state, eval 10, the matched beta and gradient pair: ratio 0.998441, cos 0.999542, rms 0.016502, all three to 1 percent or the posterior is reported as failing its own control. The previously stated re-basing onto the analytic penalty norm alone is withdrawn because that quantity is an IDENTITY, reproduced exactly by any treatment knowing the penalty weight and the beta field including one whose posterior is wrong, so it is a control that cannot fail; the cosine is the only leg carrying whether the prior pull opposed the likelihood gradient. The claim that the published triple is not self-consistent is also withdrawn: it reconciles, and the apparent 1.684x arose from pairing a plateau-state ratio and cosine with a gradient norm reported at eval 16, a different state. Docket rows D8b withdrawn and D9 refuting. BLOCKED UNTIL POST-SEND per the body.

second_opinion_2026_08_11: ADVISORY ONLY, from a second closure/UQ agent that pre-registered this item in parallel before the chief consolidated S1 onto the owning session. Nothing here overrides this proposal's own price, gate or design: est_core_min 260 and the cost_basis above are the owning session's and are left exactly as committed at ecbdc288. Two findings are handed over because the owner would want them, and one of them contradicts this file. (1) SUPPORTS this proposal's pricing, with the line number it was missing: no curvature can be salvaged from any of the three completed S1 runs, because both drivers delete the per-evaluation gradient immediately after use -- invert_lbfgsb.py line 97, os.remove(gpath), comment 'keep every 10th + eval001 (the control)'. Fourteen of sixteen gradients were discarded per run, so the L-BFGS (s,y) pairs are unreconstructible: s_k survives in the eleven beta_accept_iter*.npy files, y_k = g_(k+1) - g_k does not. The cost_basis reasoning that curvature must be bought as gradient evaluations is therefore correct AND unavoidable, not merely a design choice. Recommend the os.remove be dropped for this arm: 24 HVP gradients at 168 KB is 4 MB, and discarding second-order information to save four megabytes is what made this item expensive. (2) CONTRADICTS amendment item (4) and docket D8. The published plateau-balance triple RECONCILES; it was measured from disk at 0.998441 / 0.999542 / rms 0.016502 against the published 0.998 / 0.9995 / 0.0165, from the MATCHED pair beta_eval010.npy and grad_eval010.npy (both DV order, same run_eval call, at a state evals 11-17 agree with in J to seven digits), and the identity ||g_total|| = |g_QoI|*sqrt(1+r^2-2rc) closes to six digits. The 1.684 factor comes from combining the plateau-state ratio and cosine with ||g|| = 9.011e-06, which the trajectory table reports at EVAL 16 -- a different state; near-cancellation makes the two non-interchangeable, since ||g_total|| moves 1.6x between eval 10 and eval 16 while r and c move in the fourth decimal. This matters for the gate rather than only for the record: |g_penalty| = 2*lambda_L2*||beta-1|| is an identity that any treatment knowing lambda_L2 and beta reproduces exactly, including one whose posterior is wrong, so re-basing the control onto it removes the only part that tests the BALANCE. The cosine is the informative half. Recommend G-P4 be restored to the ratio-and-cosine form and docket D8 withdrawn. Filed as docket D9 and argued in S1_WITH_PRIORS_PREREGISTRATION.md; not corrected in place, per C3. (3) One design note, conceding a point: computing the Hessian at the EXISTING beta_final rather than at the MAP under the new prior -- as the parallel pre-registration proposed -- is the weaker choice. A Laplace posterior belongs at the MAP of the posterior being claimed. This proposal's MAP-arm-then-HVP ordering is the better-founded one and should stand.
